findings.reason: The Brief preserves the latency-reduction study, mandatory preservation of retrieval quality, and evidence-grounded report. It invents no method or numeric improvement threshold. No accepted exclusions or preferences are lost or promoted.

The single_gpu constraint exactly reflects the authorized hardware policy, is attributed as a system default, and is recorded in an assumption with its authority and affected field. The Brief explicitly avoids asserting hardware availability.

All three mandatory requirements have acceptance and evidence obligations. Both target metrics link to their corresponding requirements; the report deliverable covers the requested result. Evidence obligations require baseline-relative support, distinguish unresolved claims, and acknowledge the absence of supplied empirical measurements.

The Brief supplies an actionable study objective, qualitative targets, constraints, reference input binding, report deliverable, acceptance expectations, and traceable evidence obligations. Unchosen methods and thresholds remain explicitly nonblocking. Supplied binding-integrity checks also pass.

limitations: No empirical measurements are supplied; compilation acceptance does not establish latency improvement or retrieval-quality preservation.
The study method and numeric improvement threshold remain unchosen.
Availability of hardware matching the authorized single_gpu profile remains unverified.
